summary:
Space Base Commander is an interactive educational web application that transforms space exploration into a hands-on learning experience for children. Inspired by NASA's lunar and Martian exploration missions, the game places players in the role of a Space Commander, assisted by ASTRO, a robotic companion, as they complete five interconnected missions.

Players experiment with thermal protection materials, defend a space habitat against environmental hazards, navigate challenging planetary terrain, extract and purify underground water, and construct a permanent space base.

Through interactive simulations, resource management, scientific experimentation, and meaningful decision-making, players discover how real space exploration challenges are addressed. Decisions made in earlier missions influence later challenges, encouraging critical thinking, problem-solving, and scientific reasoning.

Our goal is to make STEM education more engaging and accessible by allowing young explorers to learn through experimentation, consequences, and discovery.
details:
Space Base Commander — Project Details

1. Project Overview

Space Base Commander is an interactive educational web application designed to introduce children to the challenges of lunar and Martian exploration through immersive gameplay, scientific experimentation, and problem-solving.

Players take on the role of a Space Commander, accompanied by ASTRO, an intelligent robotic assistant. Together, they undertake a five-mission campaign in which scientific decisions, resource management, and environmental challenges determine the success of their space exploration journey.

Players can choose between two destinations: the Moon or Mars. This choice influences the environmental conditions, scientific scenarios, hazards, and equipment used throughout the campaign.

2. How It Works — The Five Missions

The experience is organized into five interconnected missions:

Mission 1 — The Space Calling

Players prepare their spacecraft by selecting thermal protection materials and dust filtration systems. They then pilot the landing capsule, collect energy resources, and safely land on suitable terrain. Their equipment choices influence the protection available in subsequent missions.

Mission 2 — Operation: Lunar Shield / Red Storm

Players defend their space habitat against environmental hazards, including radiation spikes on the Moon or giant dust storms on Mars. They manage energy and oxygen, activate protective shields, repair damaged modules, and deploy a rover to clean solar panels.

Mission 3 — Terrain Explorer

Players navigate a topographic environment using a rover, manage battery consumption according to terrain inclination, collect geological samples, and evaluate potential locations for establishing a permanent base.

Mission 4 — Water and Ice Explorer

Players use simulated subsurface radar and drilling equipment to locate and extract underground ice or water. They manage battery levels and drill temperature before purifying the extracted water through filtration processes.

Mission 5 — Regolith Explorer

Players conduct physical soil stability experiments, compare different regolith materials, select appropriate foundations, and construct their permanent space base. Previous decisions about water purification, thermal protection, and environmental shielding influence the final construction.

3. Scientific Learning and Educational Impact

Rather than relying on traditional multiple-choice quizzes, Space Base Commander uses interactive cause-and-effect learning.

Players must observe environmental conditions, experiment with equipment, manage limited resources, make decisions, and understand the consequences of their actions.

The campaign introduces scientific concepts including:

  • Planetary environments and gravity.
  • Thermal insulation and radiation protection.
  • Solar energy and resource management.
  • Geological exploration and terrain analysis.
  • Subsurface ice detection and water purification.
  • Soil stability and habitat construction.

The application also includes a Discovery Codex, where players can review scientific discoveries, equipment, achievements, and practical lessons learned throughout the campaign.

4. NASA Inspiration and Scientific References

The project draws inspiration from NASA exploration missions and scientific instruments, including:

  • Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter (LRO), particularly LOLA, Diviner, and LROC.
  • Lunar Crater Observation and Sensing Satellite (LCROSS).
  • Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter (MRO), including SHARAD, CRISM, and HiRISE.
  • Mars Odyssey and its THEMIS instrument.
  • Mars Global Surveyor and MOLA.
  • Curiosity and Perseverance rover exploration missions.
  • NASA's Artemis program.

The current application uses educational simulations and illustrative values inspired by these scientific instruments and exploration concepts. It does not directly retrieve live NASA datasets or communicate with NASA APIs during gameplay. Simulated information is presented for educational purposes and is not intended to represent real-time planetary measurements.

5. Technologies and Implementation

Space Base Commander was developed as a client-side Single Page Application (SPA) using:

  • React 19 — Interactive user interface and component architecture.
  • TypeScript — Type-safe application logic and game state.
  • Vite 8 — Development environment and build tooling.
  • Tailwind CSS v4 — Responsive styling and accessibility features.
  • Three.js — Real-time 3D environments, procedural planetary terrain, and character models.
  • HTML5 Canvas and SVG — Interactive mission interfaces, maps, and visual simulations.
  • Web Audio API — Procedurally generated sound effects.
  • Web Speech API — Optional voice narration for ASTRO.
  • Browser localStorage — Local campaign persistence and decision memory.
  • Lucide React — Interface icons.

The application runs entirely in the browser without requiring a backend server or external AI service during gameplay.

6. Creativity, Accessibility, and Innovation

One of the project's main innovations is its interconnected campaign system. Decisions made during earlier missions are remembered and influence later scenarios, creating continuity and meaningful consequences.

The application combines 3D exploration environments with interactive 2D mission simulations, providing different gameplay experiences while maintaining a coherent educational journey.

Accessibility features include optional sound, voice narration, subtitles, and a reduced-stimuli mode that minimizes intense animations and visual effects.

Players can also personalize their commander, including appearance, spacesuit, mission emblem, and team identity.

7. Intended Impact

Space Base Commander aims to make space science more accessible, engaging, and understandable for children aged 7 to 12.

By transforming complex space exploration challenges into interactive missions, the project encourages curiosity, scientific reasoning, creativity, environmental awareness, and early interest in STEM fields.

Our vision is to help young learners experience the challenges of becoming space explorers while discovering the science and engineering behind future lunar and Martian habitats.
